## Hong Kong Mahjong (廣東麻雀)

The classic, fast-paced family game. Build four sets and a pair; your hand must be worth at least 3 fan to win.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Players** | 4 (or 3) |
| **Tiles** | 136 — no flowers |
| **To win** | 3 fan minimum |
| **Limit** | 13 fan |

### The tiles

Three suits — Dots, Bamboo and Characters — numbered 1 to 9, four copies of each. Then the honours: four Winds (East, South, West, North) and three Dragons (Red, Green, White), also four of each. Hong Kong play here uses no flower tiles.

> Suits: Dots, Bamboo, Characters: 1 of Dots · 5 of Dots · 1 of Bamboo · 7 of Bamboo · 3 of Characters · 9 of Characters

> Honours: Winds and Dragons: East Wind · South Wind · West Wind · North Wind · Red Dragon · Green Dragon · White Dragon

### A winning hand

Fourteen tiles: four sets and a pair (the "Eyes"). A set is a Chow (three in a row in one suit), a Pung (three identical tiles) or a Kong (four identical tiles — it counts as one set, and you draw a replacement tile).

> Chow · Pung · Chow · Pung · Pair: 2 of Bamboo · 3 of Bamboo · 4 of Bamboo · 7 of Dots · 7 of Dots · 7 of Dots · 5 of Characters · 6 of Characters · 7 of Characters · Red Dragon · Red Dragon · Red Dragon · East Wind · East Wind

One special hand is also complete: Thirteen Orphans (one of each 1, 9, Wind and Dragon, plus a pair of any of them). Seven Pairs is not allowed in this game.

Being complete is not enough: the hand must score at least 3 fan. A complete hand below that (a "Chicken Hand") cannot be declared.

### How a hand is played

- Everyone is dealt 13 tiles; the dealer (East) draws a 14th and discards first. Play passes to the next seat each turn.
- On your turn draw one tile from the wall, then discard one. You may declare a concealed Kong, add a fourth tile to an exposed Pung, or win on the tile you drew (Self-drawn).
- Any player may claim a discard: to win, or for a Pung or Kong. Only the next player in turn may claim it for a Chow. Priority: a win beats a Pung or Kong, which beats a Chow; several players may win on the same discard.
- A claimed set is placed face up (exposed); the claimer then discards. A Kong draws a replacement tile first.
- The hand ends when someone wins or the wall runs out (a draw game).

When another player’s discard is one you can call for a Chow, Pung or Kong, the game stops and asks you (Pass or Escape declines; Hint says what the computer would do). A winning discard is taken for you automatically. Your own draws offer Kong and Win.

### Scoring and payment

Count the fan of every pattern your hand has (see the table below), capped at 13. Fan converts to points on a doubling table.

- Self-drawn win: every other player pays you the points.
- Win on a discard: the player who discarded it pays.
- Draw game: nobody pays.

### Dealer and rounds

The dealer keeps the deal after winning or after a draw game; otherwise the deal passes to the next seat. A game is one round: the deal goes round the table once (extra hands when the dealer repeats). The highest score at the end wins.

## Riichi Mahjong (リーチ麻雀)

Japanese mahjong: every win needs at least one yaku (a scoring condition), and you can declare riichi when your closed hand is one tile from winning.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Players** | 4, or 3 (sanma) |
| **Tiles** | 136 (sanma: 108) |
| **To win** | at least 1 yaku |
| **Start** | 25,000 (sanma 35,000) |

### The tiles

Dots (pin), Bamboo (sou) and Characters (man) 1–9, four Winds and three Dragons, four copies of each — no flowers. Three-player games (sanma) remove the 2–8 of Characters.

> Pin, sou, man, winds and dragons: 1 of Dots · 5 of Bamboo · 9 of Characters · East Wind · White Dragon · Green Dragon · Red Dragon

Red fives are not used in this game.

### A winning hand

Four sets (Chi, Pon or Kan) and a pair — or Seven Pairs (seven different pairs), or Thirteen Orphans. A complete hand also needs at least one yaku from the table below; dora alone are not a yaku.

> All Simples (Tanyao): no 1s, 9s or honours: 2 of Characters · 3 of Characters · 4 of Characters · 4 of Dots · 5 of Dots · 6 of Dots · 6 of Bamboo · 7 of Bamboo · 8 of Bamboo · 6 of Dots · 7 of Dots · 8 of Dots · 5 of Bamboo · 5 of Bamboo

### Riichi

- With a closed hand that is one tile from winning (Tenpai), at least 1,000 points and tiles left in the wall, you may declare riichi with your discard and put a 1,000-point stick on the table.
- From then on your hand is locked: you discard every tile you draw unless it wins (a closed Kan is allowed only if it changes nothing about your wait).
- Riichi is itself a yaku (1 han), and winning within one go-around of declaring adds Ippatsu. Declaring on your very first discard is Double Riichi.
- The winner of the hand collects every riichi stick on the table.

### Calls, furiten and dora

- Chi only from the player on your left; Pon and Kan from anyone; Ron on anyone’s discard. You may not discard the tile you just called with (no swap-calling, kuikae).
- Furiten: if any tile you are waiting on is in your own discards — or you passed it up since your last turn, or since declaring riichi — you can’t win by Ron, only by Tsumo.
- The Dead wall holds 14 tiles. One Dora indicator is turned face up: the NEXT tile in order is the dora, worth 1 han each in a winning hand. Every Kan turns over another indicator. A riichi winner also counts the ura dora under the indicators.
- Calling any tile opens your hand: some yaku are then worth less or not available (see "closed only" below).

When another player’s discard is one you can call for a Chi, Pon or Kan, the game stops and asks you (Pass or Escape declines; Hint says what the computer would do) — never once you are in riichi. A winning discard (Ron) is taken for you automatically. Your own draws offer Tsumo, Kan, Riichi and (when allowed) the nine-terminals draw.

### Han, fu and payment

Add the han of every yaku (plus dora). Below a limit hand, points come from han and fu (fu counts the hand’s sets and wait, rounded up to 10): base = fu × 2^(han + 2). From 5 han the limits below apply; 13+ han counts as a yakuman.

- Ron: the discarder pays it all — 4 × base for a non-dealer, 6 × base for the dealer.
- Tsumo: a non-dealer gets base from each non-dealer and 2 × base from the dealer; a dealer gets 2 × base from everyone.
- Each counter (Honba) adds 300 to a Ron and 100 per payer to a Tsumo.
- Exhaustive draw: players not ready pay 3,000 in total (sanma 2,000) to those who are ready. A discard pile of only terminals and honours, never called from, pays a Mangan (Nagashi Mangan).

### Dealer, draws and the end

- The dealer keeps the deal after winning, after being ready at a draw, or after an abortive draw; each time a counter is added.
- Abortive draws: Nine Terminals, Four Winds, Four Riichi, Four Kans, Triple Ron.
- A game is one round (East). It ends early if a player drops below zero. Riichi sticks still on the table go to the leader.

## Chinese Official (国标麻将)

The international competition rules (MCR): 81 scoring fans, and a hand must be worth at least 8 points — not counting flowers — to win.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Players** | 4 (or 3) |
| **Tiles** | 144 — with 8 flowers |
| **To win** | 8 points minimum |
| **Fans** | 81 |

### The tiles

Dots, Bamboo and Characters 1–9, four Winds and three Dragons — four of each — plus eight bonus tiles: four Flowers and four Seasons.

> Suits, honours, a flower and a season: 3 of Dots · 8 of Bamboo · 6 of Characters · South Wind · Green Dragon · Flower 1 · Season 2

A flower or season is never kept in the hand: when you draw one (or are dealt one) it is set aside and you draw a replacement. Each is worth 1 point, added AFTER the 8-point minimum is checked.

### A winning hand

Four sets and a pair — or one of the special shapes: Seven Pairs, Thirteen Orphans, Lesser or Greater Honors and Knitted Tiles, or a Knitted Straight. Unlike Hong Kong, the same four tiles may count as two pairs in Seven Pairs.

> Pure Straight (16 points): 1 of Bamboo · 2 of Bamboo · 3 of Bamboo · 4 of Bamboo · 5 of Bamboo · 6 of Bamboo · 7 of Bamboo · 8 of Bamboo · 9 of Bamboo · 2 of Dots · 2 of Dots · 2 of Dots · 8 of Characters · 8 of Characters

It must score at least 8 points from fans, flowers not included. A complete hand with no fan at all is a Chicken Hand (8 points).

### How a hand is played

- Chow only from the player before you; Pung and Kong from anyone; win on anyone’s discard. Only ONE player may win on a discard — the first in turn order.
- There is no furiten: you may win on a discard even if you threw that tile away earlier.
- An added Kong (a fourth tile on an exposed Pung) can be robbed by a player who wins on that tile; a concealed Kong cannot.
- The deal passes to the next player after every hand.

When another player’s discard is one you can call for a Chow, Pung or Kong, the game stops and asks you (Pass or Escape declines; Hint says what the computer would do). A winning discard is taken for you automatically. Your own draws offer Kong and Win.

### Counting fans

- Add up every fan the hand contains; arrange the tiles in the way that scores most.
- A fan that is implied by a bigger one is not counted again (the "not also" notes below) — for example Full Flush already implies No Honors.
- Each set may combine with the others only once when counting pair relationships (Pure Double Chow, Mixed Double Chow, Short Straight…).

### Payment

- Win on a discard: the discarder pays 8 + the hand’s points; every other player pays 8.
- Self-drawn win: every other player pays 8 + the hand’s points.
- Draw game: nobody pays. Everyone starts at 0.

### Glossary

| Term | Native | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Chow | 吃 · chī | Three in a row in one suit. |
| Pung | 碰 · pèng | Three identical tiles. |
| Kong | 杠 · gàng | Four identical tiles; draw a replacement. |
| Pair | 将 · jiàng | The pair in a winning hand. |
| Hu | 和 · hú | Declaring a winning hand. |
| Self-drawn | 自摸 · zì mō | Winning on a tile you drew. |
| Minimum 8 points | 八番起和 · bā fān qǐ hú | A hand must score 8 points from fans to win. |
| Flower | 花牌 · huā pái | A bonus tile, set aside when drawn. |
| Base payment (8 points) | 底分 · dǐ fēn | What every loser pays the winner. |
| Chicken Hand | 无番和 · wú fān hú | A complete hand with no other fan. |
| False win | 错和 · cuò hú | Declaring a win that isn’t valid. |
| Replacement tile | 补花 · bǔ huā | The tile drawn after a flower or a Kong. |
